t: Memory Resource Monitor - public implementations survey
title: Memory Resource Monitor - public implementations survey
definition: Tracks system and process memory consumption.
description:
Memory Resource Monitor is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Tracks system and process memory consumption. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Memory Resource Monitor. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Memory Resource Monitor. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Memory Resource Monitor capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: SSH - related Memory Resource Monitor technology
title: SSH - related Memory Resource Monitor technology
definition: Encrypted remote shell.
description:
SSH is not itself a Memory Resource Monitor, but it belongs in this survey because real Memory Resource Monitor work leans on it. Encrypted remote shell.

In a Memory Resource Monitor build it shows up when the team already lives in its ecosystem. Its architecture reflects hard-won lessons: small sharp pieces, explicit contracts between them, and no magic hidden from the operator. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Memory Resource Monitor practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, SSH is the pragmatic pick for most builds as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Memory Resource Monitor from a one-paragraph brief
